messages:
kim_nguyen: Heads up — I found weird KMS unwrap activity from svc-async-handler hitting workspaces it shouldn't. Might be related to the RBAC change we merged yesterday. tagging @raj_patel @sasha :eyes:

raj_patel: Can you paste the log snippet and the workspace IDs?

kim_nguyen: Paste below — redacted IDs but shows sequence and header oddness:
```
2026-03-19T14:02:11Z svc=svc-async-handler req_id=aa12 unwrap workspace_id=ws-57 target_key=key-prod-1 result=OK
2026-03-19T14:02:12Z svc=svc-async-handler req_id=aa13 unwrap workspace_id=workspace=null target_key=key-prod-2 result=PERMISSION_DENIED
2026-03-19T14:02:13Z svc=svc-async-handler req_id=aa14 unwrap workspace_id=ws-99 target_key=key-staging result=OK
```
Two successes where workspace headers looked present and one where header is null but DENIED. The odd thing: ws-99 belongs to a different org than svc-async-handler's default org.

sasha: Wait — we merged the role inheritance refactor (PR #3421) that flattened org->project permissions. Could that have unintentionally allowed project-level kms.unwrap to be evaluated on requests routed from other workspaces? @elaine_m implemented the change.

elaine_m: I did the flattening to simplify policy evaluation. PR notes said we kept the workspace scoping check, but I see in the runtime patch I added a short-circuit that pulls principal scope before we rehydrate workspace metadata. Possible race where header is absent and we fall back to principal's allowed projects.

max_cole: If principal auth falls back to org-wide grants, that could explain cross-workspace unwrap. Quick mitigation: revoke kms.unwrap for svc-async-handler until we patch.

raj_patel: Agreed. Also need to run an audit query across audit logs for similar unwraps.
Suggested query (psuedo):
```sql
SELECT timestamp, principal, workspace_id, key, result 
FROM audit.kms_unwrap_logs 
WHERE principal = 'svc-async-handler' AND timestamp >= '2026-03-19T00:00:00Z'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC;
```

kim_nguyen: Ran it — 3 successes total; one maps to ws-57 (our internal test org), one maps to ws-99 (customer X), one maps to ws-12 (staging). We need to determine whether any plaintext key material was returned for a customer key.

deploy-bot: [deploy-notify] Canary deploy applied: service/runtime-authenticator v2.4.1 (PR #3421) by elaine_m — 2026-03-19T12:58:00Z

sasha: We should roll back PR #3421 in staging and hold prod. If rollback not possible fast, add a runtime guard to ensure workspace header is required for KMS unwrap calls.

elaine_m: I can ship a hotfix to re-check request headers before fallback. Opening hotfix CH-3456. Will patch in 10m.

max_cole: For immediate ACL: run:
```bash
# revoke unwrap from principal until patch
redwoodctl iam revoke --principal svc-async-handler --perm kms.unwrap --scope project:all
# verify
redwoodctl iam list --principal svc-async-handler
```
I can run if someone makes the call.

raj_patel: Also capture KMS server-side unwrap logs and cross-check key IDs with customer ownership via Key Registry. If any customer key was unwrapped under wrong org, escalate to incident response and compliance.

kim_nguyen: I've reached out to compliance and started mapping key IDs. So far keys for ws-99 look like belonging to customer org-88. I don't yet know if plaintext got returned — KMS audit shows success but payload column is not in the public log. Need secure audit export.

elaine_m: Hotfix pushed to canary (CH-3456). It enforces presence of `x-workspace-id` in runtime before any KMS call, and returns 403 if missing.

deploy-bot: [deploy-notify] Hotfix deploy: runtime-authenticator v2.4.2-rc1 (CH-3456) by elaine_m — 2026-03-19T15:12:05Z

max_cole: After hotfix, we should rotate affected keys if we confirm customer keys were unwrapped. Also consider KMS policy change to require explicit key binding to workspace scope.

raj_patel: I'll run the audit query across 30 days to ensure this was a one-off. Also preparing the incident triage doc template.

kim_nguyen: I'll own customer comms if we need to notify. For now, action items: 1) revoke unwrap from svc-async-handler (max to run) 2) confirm whether any customer key plaintext was returned (raj -> compliance) 3) patch in prod if canary good (elaine) 4) open postmortem and update PR guardrails (sasha).

sasha: Good. Also add a unit test to ensure runtime requires workspace header for KMS calls.

elaine_m: Will add test.

kim_nguyen: Thanks all. Keeping this thread updated — will post final audit results here. :lock:
